_comment: ACK LEDGER for scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh _check_launchd_agents (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION, 2026-07-23). A listed `label` whose launchd check currently fails (not-loaded OR non-zero exit status) is reported as acknowledged-degraded instead of a fresh failure: if every unhealthy launchd label found this run is in this list, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (with the acknowledged labels named in `detail` for transparency) so the Tier-1 cron does not re-spawn system-auditor every ~30min tick re-confirming a signature that already has an open backlog fix-task. A NEW/unacknowledged failure (label absent from this list) always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — acknowledgment never masks a fresh signature. STALENESS RULE: remove an entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED — a stale entry left here after the underlying fix ships would silently re-suppress a REAL regression forever. THE STALENESS RULE IS NOW CODE-ENFORCED, not prose-only (FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY, 2026-07-29): `_launchd_label_acked()` resolves `tracked_by` against every docs/data/orch/orch-state.json task_board lane on every probe run — an entry whose `tracked_by` is absent from every lane, OR has reached DONE_VERIFIED, no longer suppresses; the probe reports it as a fresh STALE-ACK failure instead. You may still remove a stale entry by hand for tidiness, but leaving one here past its tracked task's DONE_VERIFIED no longer silently re-suppresses anything. Read-only from the probe's point of view; edited by hand (PO/developer) when a launchd death gets triaged into a tracked backlog row, or when that row closes.

THE LABEL IS STILL UNHEALTHY, FOR A THIRD AND COMPLETELY DIFFERENT REASON: it is now `not-loaded` because the ROUTER DELIBERATELY DISARMED IT on explicit user instruction. Verified independently by PO: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.vn-market.fleet-push.plist carries Disabled => 1. NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-CHECKING THIS: that file is a BINARY plist — `grep -i disabled` returns NOTHING and reads as absent. Use `plutil -p`. PO hit that exact false negative before re-checking and briefly concluded the disarm was not in the plist at all. WHY THE ENTRY IS NOT REMOVED TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT RETARGETED EITHER. Retargeting to a convenient open row is FORBIDDEN by this ledger and the rag-service entry records that precise mistake being made and corrected — the router proposed the constraint and PO agrees. Bare removal today is also wrong, but NOT for the usual reason: it would flip Tier-1 to FAILURE every 30 minutes on a state the USER CHOSE, and the per-signature spawn debounce that would bound that churn is only HALF wired (scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh now emits spawn_decision, but the consumer at .claude/skills/cron-detect-loop/register.md:84 still branches on `verdict` and never reads it), so the churn would be real at roughly 48 system-auditor respawns/day. THE ORDER IS THEREFORE: (1) ship FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-SPAWN-DEBOUNCE-2-FLOWDOC-CRON-PROMPT — promoted to ready[], P0, deps released, dispatchable now — which bounds the churn; (2) then remove this entry per the STALENESS RULE. That is not a new protocol invented here: it is verbatim the protocol this ledger already wrote for the rag-service entry in expiry_hazard_20260824T0716Z. THE DURABLE FIX IS A PROBE CHANGE, NOT A LEDGER ENTRY: a label whose loaded plist carries Disabled=1 is deliberately disabled and must be scored EXPECTED-DISABLED, never degraded — deterministic, self-expiring on re-arm, no tracked_by, no staleness risk. Minted as FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-SCORES-DELIBERATELY-DISABLED-LAUNCHD-JOB-AS-DEGRADED (backlog, P1, developer). An ack is simply the wrong instrument for a policy decision: this ledger acknowledges DEGRADED things that have an open fix row, and a deliberately disarmed job is not degraded and has nothing to fix. TRACKED_BY DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCHANGED: FIX-SIZELINT-PUSHBCTCLAYOUTHANDLER-252L-BLOCKS-ENTIRE-FLEET-PUSH was moved in_progress -> review[] (next_agent=qa) by PO this tick and is NOT yet DONE_VERIFIED, so `_launchd_label_acked()` still resolves it as present-and-open and this entry still suppresses — behaviour is unchanged by that lane move. The moment QA certifies it, the code-enforced STALENESS RULE fires automatically and the churn arrives. That sequencing constraint is recorded on the row itself so QA sees it before flipping.

_comment_acked_memory: ACK LEDGER for the SAME probe's _check_mem_creep (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE, 2026-07-25). A listed `container` value is matched (case-insensitive substring) against the full name of any RUNNING, memory-capped container whose docker-stats MemPerc breaches WARN_PCT=85: if every breaching container this run is covered, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (acked containers named in `detail` for transparency). A breach NOT covered here always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — same mixed-case-never-suppresses guarantee as `acked` above. STALENESS RULE identical: remove the entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED. Seeded 2026-07-25 with rag-service, whose high steady-state (~94-98% of its 768m cap, healthy/serving throughout) is a detector-scope question, not a detector defect. CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (PO): the seed originally named RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND as the root cause of that steady-state. That was WRONG and is refuted by measurement — see the entry retarget_reason below. The driver is the embedder model singleton (fixed ~700 MiB baseline reached on the first embed), whose ceiling trade is owned by FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY, with the compaction failure-path counter defect owned by FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP. THE STALENESS RULE AND THE ABSOLUTE-HEADROOM GAP ARE NOW BOTH CODE-ENFORCED (FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY, 2026-07-29, supersedes the 'tracked_by is never read' / 'unbounded in both directions' language that was accurate before this fix): `_mem_container_acked()` now (a) resolves `tracked_by` against every orch-state.json task_board lane every run — absent-from-every-lane or DONE_VERIFIED means the entry is a STALE ACK and stops suppressing; (b) computes absolute headroom (cap - usage) and refuses to suppress once it drops below MEM_FLOOR_MIB=40 (calibrated against rag-service's own ~20 MiB measured compact()-failure burst, see FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP, not the cap). See `floor_enforcement_20260729` on the rag-service entry below for the live consequence this has on THIS specific entry. Do NOT resolve staleness via a per-container threshold override (PO DECISION, task FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE: static overrides are the same lagging-whitelist failure mode as FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX and would also silently swallow a REAL rag OOM approach) — MEM_FLOOR_MIB is a single global constant, deliberately not per-container. RE-BASED 2026-08-24 (po/ruling-20260824T0716Z): this comment's '~94-98% of its 768m cap' figure and every percentage on the rag-service entry below are against a DEAD DENOMINATOR -- the cap was raised to 2 GiB on 2026-08-23 by FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY. Read `cap_rebase_20260824T0716Z` and `expiry_hazard_20260824T0716Z` on that entry FIRST. Also standing, unchanged by the re-base: PO refused a pdf-extractor entry here twice (2026-08-24T04:00Z and T07:16Z) -- an ack hides the SIGNAL, a per-signature spawn debounce hides only the DUPLICATE SPAWN, and MemPerc-derived headroom overstates this container's true cgroup headroom by ~100x so MEM_FLOOR_MIB could never bound such an ack. ★ DECISIVE ANTI-ACK EVIDENCE, added 2026-08-24T07:22Z (po/ruling-20260824T0722Z) — read this before any future attempt to add pdf-extractor here: kernel dmesg, read via the read-only nsenter recipe on FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY status_note, shows TWO REAL CONSTRAINT_MEMCG OOM KILLS of pdf-extractor python3 worker processes on 2026-08-23 at 14:27:11Z and 14:58:52Z (anon-rss 2,484,996 kB and 2,468,832 kB against the 2,684,354,560 B cap), on the container instance that preceded the current one. Docker sets .State.OOMKilled=true only for the container MAIN pid, so a killed CHILD leaves OOMKilled=false / ExitCode=0 / RestartCount=0 — every docker-plane probe read clean while the kernel was killing workers, the same false-negative class recorded on FIX-RAG-LANCECORE-OOM-PERSISTS-AFTER-THREADPIN-DEPLOYED. The Tier-1 mem_creep FAILURE on pdf-extractor is therefore a TRUE POSITIVE, and an entry here would silence a LIVE CRASH SOURCE, not a benign steady state. The respawn churn is fixed by FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FOLD-VERDICT-NOT-DURABLE-RESPAWNS-AUDITOR-EVERY-TICK (per-signature SPAWN debounce, verdict stays RED), never by an ack. Note the ring buffer ROLLS (an earlier 2026-08-20T11:01Z pdf-extractor hit already aged out) — absence of hits only proves absence across the buffer live span, so re-read before citing a clean result.

acked_memory.retarget_reason: SCOPE MISMATCH + UNREACHABLE SELF-EXPIRY. (1) The prior tracked_by, RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND, bounds _build_fts_index(). It is NOT the driver of the suppressed condition: rag-service reaches ~97% of its 768 MiB cap after a SINGLE embed, with zero FTS activity, because apps/rag-service/infrastructure/embedder.py holds the sentence-transformers model as a lazy singleton with no release path (MEASURED by PO 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z: cold RSS 50.7 MiB -> 749.9 MiB after one POST /index; re-measured 756.8 MiB at 11:47Z, i.e. a FIXED anonymous baseline that does not scale with request volume — see memory_split_20260729 below for the cgroup split that establishes this, and note the earlier wording here said 745.8 MiB / flat, which was a stale two-sample reading corrected the same tick). Shipping the FTS row would not lower the number. That row own 2026-07-15 qa_result.idle_baseline_flag already said so verbatim: idle mem ~92% of the 768m bound with ZERO FTS activity — ten days before this ledger was seeded against it. (2) The STALENESS RULE is this ledger only safety promise, and binding it to RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND made it unreachable: that row is blocked_on rag-corpus-repopulation-to-representative-scale, PO-projected testable on/after ~2026-08-16, po_timegate_next_recheck_after 2026-08-12. The ACK could not expire for >=18 days by construction. FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY owns the resident-set / 768m-cap trade, so its DONE_VERIFIED is the event that would genuinely mean rag-service no longer sits at 97% of its cap. ENTRY DELIBERATELY NOT REMOVED: removal flips Tier-1 to FAILURE every ~30min tick and re-spawns system-auditor ~48x/day to re-confirm a known condition — the exact churn FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION was minted to kill. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE FIELD: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:275 reads ONLY .acked_memory[].container. tracked_by is read by nothing, so this retarget changes NO probe behaviour and the STALENESS RULE remains enforced by prose alone. Making tracked_by load-bearing, plus an absolute-headroom floor the ACK may not swallow, is FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY (backlog, P1).
acked_memory.memory_split_20260729: CGROUP anon/file SPLIT — this is the measurement that decides whether the suppressed condition is dangerous, so it lives here rather than only on the task rows. At the 10:12Z restart the cgroup read anon = 761716736 B (726.4 MiB) immediately pre-restart against ~767 MiB total usage, falling to anon = 32272384 B (30.8 MiB) immediately post-restart. ANON IS ~95% OF THE CGROUP; FILE-BACKED IS AT MOST ~40 MiB. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYONE REVIEWING THIS SUPPRESSION: the memory is process-resident, NOT reclaimable page cache. There is no kernel reclaim that will rescue this container under pressure, and the ~11 MiB of headroom recorded above is genuinely all there is against a compaction burst documented at ~20 MiB. An earlier reading on the task rows argued the opposite (that a 786 MiB on-disk LanceDB corpus was filling the cgroup as file cache) — that is RETRACTED; 786 MiB on disk versus a 768 MiB cap is a numeric coincidence, not a mechanism, and the corpus is not resident here. PROVENANCE: the two anon figures are router-supplied and were NOT independently re-derived by PO — re-deriving requires reading the VM cgroup tree, and the only route available is a docker exec, which is what allocated inside this cgroup and SIGKILLed the container at 10:12Z (exec exit 137, RestartCount 21->22). DO NOT RE-RUN IT TO CONFIRM. It is independently corroborated in mechanism by a measurement already on FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP: cold RSS 50.7 MiB rising to 749.9 MiB after a SINGLE POST /index, with the model load logged 10:24:28.5Z-10:24:48.9Z — a 699 MiB step from one embed can only be anonymous heap.
acked_memory.suppression_still_warranted: YES as of 2026-07-29T11:50Z, and the reasoning is unchanged by the correction above: the condition is a known, tracked, steady-state consequence of a no-release-path model singleton, and removing this entry would flip Tier-1 to FAILURE every ~30min tick and re-spawn system-auditor ~48x/day to re-confirm it. BUT THE MARGIN IS THINNER THAN THIS LEDGER PREVIOUSLY IMPLIED and the suppression is currently unbounded in both directions: there is no absolute-headroom floor below which the ACK stops suppressing, and tracked_by is read by no code so the entry cannot self-expire. Both are tracked by FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY (backlog, P1). RE-REVIEW THIS ENTRY, do not assume it: if headroom falls below ~5 MiB, or RestartCount/day climbs above ~5 (it is 22 total over 13.8 days = 1.6/day, unmoved since 10:12:01Z), the suppression is no longer appropriate and the entry should be pulled even though its tracked_by row is still open.
acked_memory.floor_enforcement_20260729: FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY LANDED — both gaps `suppression_still_warranted` above flagged as unbounded are now code-enforced (MEM_FLOOR_MIB=40, tracked_by resolved against orch-state.json). LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS EXACT ENTRY: `headroom_mib_at_ack_review` above is 11.2 MiB, well below the 40 MiB floor, while `tracked_by`=FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY currently resolves to a live (BACKLOG, non-DONE_VERIFIED) status — so the entry fails on the BELOW-FLOOR predicate specifically, not staleness. As of this fix landing, the NEXT Tier-1 tick that samples rag-service at or near this headroom will report verdict FAILURE (detail names rag-service, its %, its MiB-free, and BELOW-FLOOR), not ALL_GREEN. THIS IS THE INTENDED, DESIGNED OUTCOME of the fix (its AC2), not a regression: the whole point of this row was that the old all-or-nothing pct>=85 predicate could not distinguish this entry's acknowledged 94-98% steady-state from the genuinely dangerous approach to 0 MiB free that is now measured live. Do not silently raise MEM_FLOOR_MIB or re-widen this ACK to make the FAILURE go away — that would recreate exactly the blind suppression this row exists to close; if the resulting cron churn needs managing, route it to PO for a capacity/cap decision (FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY), not a detector change.
acked_memory.cap_rebase_20260824T0716Z: CAP RE-BASE (po/ruling-20260824T0716Z). Every percentage in this entry -- and in retarget_reason, memory_split_20260729, suppression_still_warranted and floor_enforcement_20260729 below -- was computed against a 768 MiB cap that NO LONGER EXISTS. FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY raised it to 2 GiB, deployed 2026-08-23. LIVE RE-MEASURE 2026-08-24T07:12Z: HostConfig.Memory=2147483648 B (2048 MiB); docker stats 1.83GiB/2GiB = 91.50%; therefore _mem_headroom_mib() = 2048*(100-91.50)/100 = 174.1 MiB -- 15.5x the 11.2 MiB this entry recorded, and 4.4x MEM_FLOOR_MIB=40. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, same window: system-auditor A-30 deep probe 06:39:03-06:40:18Z, 6 samples all 90.72%, VmHWM 1641088 KB (1602.6 MiB), OOMKilled=false before and after, RestartCount=0, StartedAt 2026-08-15T10:16:22Z = 9 days uptime with ZERO restarts. That kills this entry's 'RestartCount 22 over 13.8 days = 1.6/day' figure and its own stated pull-trigger ('RestartCount/day above ~5'). WHAT THIS CHANGES IN CODE: NOTHING. _check_mem_creep computes headroom LIVE from docker inspect cap + docker stats MemPerc; headroom_mib_at_ack_review is read by NO code (same class as the tracked_by-is-read-by-nothing caveat this entry used to carry, which IS now fixed). This is a documentation re-base so the next reader is not reasoning off a dead denominator. CONSEQUENCE FOR floor_enforcement_20260729: its prediction ('the NEXT Tier-1 tick that samples rag-service at or near this headroom will report verdict FAILURE ... BELOW-FLOOR') has been FALSE since the cap raise -- at 174.1 MiB the floor cannot fire. The live 07:00Z probe confirms it: rag-service appears in the '(also acknowledged-degraded, tracked: ...)' clause, i.e. SUPPRESSED, while pdf-extractor is the sole breach. SUPPRESSION STILL WARRANTED: YES, but on a NEW basis -- no longer 'thin margin, tracked', now 'high steady-state fraction of a deliberately-oversized cap, 9 days OOM-free'. The 2026-07-29 danger reading (anon ~95% of cgroup, ~11 MiB against a measured ~20 MiB compaction burst) does NOT carry over; do not re-cite memory_split_20260729's figures as live risk without re-measuring against 2048 MiB, and DO NOT re-run a docker exec to re-derive them -- that is what SIGKILLed this container on 2026-07-29 (exec exit 137, RestartCount 21->22).
acked_memory.expiry_hazard_20260824T0716Z: EXPIRY IS IMMINENT AND WILL RE-ARM A RESPAWN LOOP -- read this before closing FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY. tracked_by=FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY is the cap-raise row ITSELF, and it now sits in task_board.qa[], P0, next_agent=qa, updated_by=qa/verify-committed-20260823T1437Z -- one sign-off from DONE_VERIFIED. If it has not, remove it anyway and accept the churn -- an ack whose tracked row is DONE_VERIFIED is exactly the silent re-suppression of a real regression that the STALENESS RULE exists to prevent. NOTE also_tracked_by=FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP resolves to NO lane on the live board (cold-evicted, same shape as the com.vn-market.fleet-push acked[] entry documented above).
